name: crypto
description: Local cryptography: Convex ECIES, Ed25519 signatures and JWTs, byte hashes and secret-backed BIP39 recovery phrases and derivation.

content.inline:
## Cryptography
Choose callables from the current tool palette by descriptions and schemas.
- Generate keys and mnemonic phrases into named secrets; use the returned s/NAME reference. Never put private material into prompts, workspace data or agent config.
- To import existing material use the secret storage tool securely, then pass its reference. Ed25519 seeds are 32-byte hex; BIP39 mnemonics are English phrases. These are different formats.
- Derive-key validates the phrase checksum before deriving. Default m/44/864/0/0/0 matches Convex CLI and GetMine venue identity; m/44/864/1/0/0 matches GetMine install DID. 864 is the official Convex SLIP-44 coin type and only the default: any valid purpose, coin type and path shape is accepted, for example m/44/1234567/0/0/0 or m/7/1234567/2147483647. All components are hardened, with or without apostrophes. GetMine uses no BIP39 passphrase. m explicitly selects the SLIP-10 master for legacy recovery.
- Hash/sign/verify/encrypt accept native blob data. In JSON tool calls, use 0x-prefixed hex by default; text requires encoding:utf8 or encoding:base64. There is no implicit hash or CAD3 conversion. To sign a CAD3 hash, obtain the intended value hash and pass that hash blob directly, or its 0x-prefixed JSON representation. SHA3-256 and Keccak-256 are different.
- Digests, public keys, signatures and ciphertext are native blobs; Convex renders them as 0x-prefixed lowercase hex at the JSON boundary, not PEM. ECIES uses the Convex HPKE envelope; it does not prove sender identity.
- Decrypt returns a native plaintext blob by default. Supply name to keep plaintext in the secret store (hex by default, because SecretStore stores strings); select encoding:utf8 explicitly to store decoded text. Omitting name returns plaintext into job output and potentially model history. Explicit utf8/hex/base64 modes return encoded text.
- Existing secrets are protected unless overwrite:true is explicitly requested. Recovery phrases are not displayed by these tools; secure human backup/export needs a separate trusted interface.
- Invocation authority is required. Generated secret writes need secret/write. Cross-user secret references require secret/use; destination-bound grants cannot authorise local crypto. Derive-key reads only your own secrets.
- JWT sign accepts a claims map and a seed secret reference. It uses EdDSA (Ed25519), adds no claims or expiry, and returns an AString compact token. Supply name to store a bearer token directly as a secret; otherwise it enters Job output. Use Unix seconds for exp/nbf/iat, not milliseconds.
- JWT verify requires an independently trusted accountKey (Blob or hex). Supply expectedIssuer and expectedAudience for the application and requireExpiration:true for expiring access tokens. It checks exp/nbf when present; iat is descriptive. Only valid:true results contain verified claims. Token headers never select a key. No HS256/RS256 or critical JOSE extensions are supported here.
- JWT verify/decode take exactly one of token (compact text) or tokenSecret (secret reference). JWT decode always returns verified:false; decoded claims cannot establish identity or access. These crypto operations do not authenticate venue callers or authorize capabilities; use the auth system and UCAN tools for those policies.
- Raw JWT inputs and signing claims are redacted from recorded inputs, but successful verification/decode outputs disclose claims. Decode never returns a stored token's signature. Use stored token references with bearerSecret for downstream HTTP calls when inspection is unnecessary.
